# Product & Experience Framing — executable v0.1 slice

**Status:** runnable QA packets and spec compilation in this repository; **not** yet a CGM-installed module or an ABA runtime integration. No website, app, image or deployment was generated by this work.
**Related:** [full design](../design/PEF_HUMAN_IN_LOOP_EXPERIENCE_ROUTER.md), [router](router.v1.json), [source run](run.schema.json), [context protocol](CONTEXT_PROTOCOL.md).

## Responsibility and limits

This module's intent is to extract a product's **actual source-owned purpose**, distinguish that from **unproven buyer/user motives**, route ambiguous consequential decisions to the owner, then design the **buyer-belief story** and (where interactions exist) **user tasks + service behavior**. It outputs a locked experience contract for [App Builder Automation](https://github.com/Pukujan/app-builder-automation).

ABA alone owns runnable frontend implementation, selected framework, tools, plan/build loops and browser checks. CGM's \`html-demo\` must not be used as a competing frontend-building route. PEF may use existing CGM brand, writing, visual and image modules after the creative strategy is accepted. A contract compilation is **not** permission to execute ABA or deploy.

### Pipeline

~~~text
S0 scope → S1 verified product truth → S2 human intent / need hypothesis
                                      │
                          Uncertainty triage and owner QA
                          (only if consequential ambiguity)
                                      │
S3 competing positions + explicit choice → S4 buyer and UX/service story
                                      │
                          Owner/editor accepts direction
                                      │
S5 exact Experience Brief and final owner creative signoff
                                      │
                      Source/QA/scene/CTA fail-closed compilation
                                      │
           ABA-spec Markdown + provenance/approval/hash manifest
                                      │
                    ABA build (NOT automated here)
                                      │
         S6 actual browser / semantic / user task / media QA
                                      │
                           Human final acceptance
~~~

**Use the existing seven run stages.** The new \`pef.py\` makes targeted QA and S5→ABA handoff concrete; it does not replace \`frame.py\` or generate strategy automatically. Generating research, market positions and story drafts is an *agent job*, not a deterministic Python rule.

## 1. Set up a run and source facts

~~~bash
python scripts/frame.py init \
  --run-id repo-v1 --project-id repo \
  --repo https://github.com/OWNER/REPO \
  --ref FULL_40_CHARACTER_GIT_COMMIT_SHA \
  --subject "Actual scoped product" \
  --objective "Discover a credible human-centered framing and task experience" \
  --out /private/path/repo-v1.json
~~~

A public run may only carry public-safe facts. Each relevant fact has an observed/owner/inferred/proposed status, scoped sources and optional \`evidence_domain\`:
- \`product_mechanism\` for observed product specification/behavior;
- \`customer_research\` **only** for observed user interviews, observation or meaningful research;
- \`owner_direction\` for approved/claimed creator purpose or strategic preference;
- \`external_context\` for market/industry context;
- \`other\` when none fits.

**A technical source cannot prove customer demand.** The validator requires \`customer_research\`-tagged observed fact(s) before a need can be labelled \`observed_user_research\`, though the classification must still be checked by a human.

## 2. Generate a *small* owner QA packet

The agent researches first, then writes a QA file according to [pef-questions.schema.json](pef-questions.schema.json) only for unresolved choices that affect product meaning, positioning, important UX states, service safety or truth. Example: [ACS B open questions](../examples/acs-version-b.questions.json) — **demonstration only, not a new owner request**.

~~~bash
python scripts/pef.py validate-qa \
  examples/acs-version-b.run.json \
  examples/acs-version-b.questions.json

python scripts/pef.py questions \
  examples/acs-version-b.run.json \
  examples/acs-version-b.questions.json \
  > /tmp/pef-review-packet.json
~~~

The packet lists at most **three** unanswered questions, highest blocking/impact first. It includes the agent's recommended option, alternative tradeoffs, source references and what will change. It records the number of remaining unresolved questions and total blocking questions.

Use a conversational question when only one essential thing is uncertain. A form becomes appropriate only when multiple distinct, genuinely necessary decisions can be answered together. Never ask a user to fill the whole research brief; the agent is responsible for preparing it.

### How an answer becomes durable

For a resolved QA item, set:
- \`status: answered\`;
- \`answer.choice_id\` from the question's choices;
- \`answer.answered_by\` and \`answer.answer_ref\` grounded in the actual owner review;
- \`answer.note\` describing correction for \`choice_id: other\`.

**An answer is not automatically a positioning/story/creative approval.** The agent must update affected decisions with traceable reviewer acceptance and evidence, or leave them proposed. A changed upstream choice invalidates dependent scenes/visuals and revisits the earliest assumption, not just the rendered CSS. \`frame.py invalidate\` can mark linked decisions/scenes stale.

If a blocking item remains unanswered or deferred, generation stops. A nonblocking item may remain deferred but is not silently promoted to true. Critical-risk items must be blocking.

## 3. Agent fills an Experience Brief (not the owner)

The agent compiles the accepted product and design decisions into [pef-experience.schema.json](pef-experience.schema.json):

- creator's purpose, independently observed user need **or explicitly labelled hypothesis**;
- lead actor/job/trigger/workaround;
- owner-accepted positioning decision and exactly permitted promise;
- buyer-belief scene order and linked actual claim IDs;
- task scenarios and interaction states (when interactive);
- service blueprint touchpoints, authority, limitations and CTA side effects;
- locked page headline/outline, visual roles, relevant accessibility/interaction acceptance;
- **actual** creative approval identity/ref matching S5.

Do not include private customer notes or private repo implementation snippets in a public example. The precise source revision must be a pinned 40-character SHA, not \`main\`.

An ordinary model can fill most of this from verified source and prior decisions. If it invents a buyer, outcomes or system actions, it fails review.

## 4. Compile the ABA input only after S3/S4/S5 acceptance

~~~bash
python scripts/pef.py check-brief \
  /private/path/repo-v1.json \
  /private/path/repo-questions.json \
  /private/path/experience.json

python scripts/pef.py compile-aba \
  /private/path/repo-v1.json \
  /private/path/repo-questions.json \
  /private/path/experience.json \
  --out /private/path/aba-input.md
~~~

The compiler:
- runs the original framing record structural checks;
- requires all S0–S5 gates accepted, with explicit S3, S4 **and S5** owner signoffs;
- requires a concrete pinned source SHA and matching brief revision/run ID;
- blocks unresolved high-impact **blocking** QA;
- requires the positioning decision to be accepted; dependent belief scenes to be accepted; public claims to be source-linked and verified;
- refuses to label a technical fact or owner direction as observed customer research;
- checks UX task/service trace references; prevents unverified CTA behavior from reaching ABA;
- requires the brief reviewer/ref to match the S5 gate;
- produces an **isolated markdown build specification** plus a sidecar \`.manifest.json\` with deterministic SHA-256 hashes of the source run, QA, brief, and output, explicitly marked \`compiled_not_executed\`, \`deployment_authorized: false\`;
- **refuses to overwrite** prior generated specs or manifests.

This is a **structural and recorded-approval gate**, not cryptographic verification of human identity, marketing desirability or actual network behavior. A malicious agent can still invent a reference; the operator must verify the cited source and reviewer action. Real external user studies cannot be replaced by static schema checks.

## ABA integration status — separate repo, review pending

A draft, opt-in adapter is proposed for the dedicated App Builder Automation repository in **its issue #60 and draft PR #61**. It validates PEF input/manifest/source approvals before work, runs a plan-only phase, saves a plan/blueprint digest, requires a recorded human approval of the exact plan, and only then resumes the same workspace for implementation. The normal unattended ABA path remains available for non-PEF work; compiled PEF input is rejected on that legacy path.

**Verification:** the dedicated PEF offline GitHub Actions job on the ABA branch passed its syntax, Python/Node digest-parity and negative-gate checks. This is a **branch proposal**, not a merged/released module or a live end-to-end product test. The general ABA CI/merge gate and PCM issue/checkpoint reconciliation remain separate. Do not claim ABA currently runs this flow on its default branch, and do not use it to build ACS B without accepted human framing decisions.

## 5. ABA handoff and verification — boundary remains manual

The current ABA runner accepts its own specification/prompt and implements a plan/blueprint/build loop. This repo does **not** yet call that runner or enforce agreement between the internal ABA blueprint and the approved PEF brief.

**Required adapter next:** pass the compiled spec to ABA's real supported CLI, compare the generated blueprint against accepted headline/positioning/behavior/CTA constraints, halt if semantics diverge, only then build. ABA owns generation and browser screenshot verification. PEF's reviewer owns source-truth and semantic/UX experience review. Human editorial signoff remains separate from green scripts.

For now the compiled Markdown is a real, reviewable **handoff artifact**, not an unattended site generator. Never treat an automated builder's self-declared approval as the owner signing the Experience Brief.

## 6. Regression tests and review

~~~bash
python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py' -v
python scripts/frame.py validate examples/acs-version-b.run.json
python scripts/pef.py validate-qa examples/acs-version-b.run.json examples/acs-version-b.questions.json
python scripts/pef.py questions examples/acs-version-b.run.json examples/acs-version-b.questions.json
~~~

Tests include accepted synthetic test fixture compilation and refusal for drafts, unpinned sources, unaccepted decisions/story scenes, missing owner approvals, owner direction passed off as user research, inferred technical facts passed off as customer research, unverified marketing claims, unverified CTA side effects, and missing service trace. The synthetic fixture's reviewer names are *tests*, not evidence of a real person's approval.

### What this slice does not provide

No actual live customer interviews or independent UX study, no automated inference of owner intent from a repo, no complete graphic storyboarding model, no automated form UI, no real execution of ABA, no builder blueprint-parity enforcement, no image/video generation, and no deployment. Those are separately testable increments, not properties we should claim have already shipped.

**Status of ACS B:** draft source, unanswered QA, unchanged Version A, **no generation authorization**.
